faq: Do I need a particular plan for custom code?

Code injection needs a Core plan or higher, depending on your Squarespace version. We check your plan first. Custom CSS in the design panel works on more plans, and we tell you what is possible before starting.
Will custom code break when Squarespace updates?
It can in rare cases, because Squarespace changes its own code. We write to stable class names where we can, comment each block and leave notes so a fix is quick if something shifts.
Can you add a third-party widget?
Yes, for booking, reviews, chat and similar tools, as long as the tool's own terms allow embedding. We style it to match your site and load it so it does not slow the page.
Can you fix code another developer left?

Yes, if it lives in your Squarespace code areas. We find what is wrong, fix it and write down the change. If the code is heavily tangled, we may suggest rewriting that part for lower cost in the long run.
desc:
Squarespace custom CSS and code covers the changes the style panel cannot make: precise spacing, hover effects, small scripts and embedded widgets. Ecom Swift LLC writes short, commented code, tests it on phone and desktop, and places it where Squarespace expects it.

## What is custom CSS and code on Squarespace?

Custom CSS and code on Squarespace means adding your own style rules, scripts or embeds to a site on top of what the editor offers. Style rules live in the Custom CSS panel. Scripts and tracking snippets go into code injection in the header or footer, or into a code block on a single page.

Used sparingly, code lets a site match a brand exactly instead of looking like every other template.

## Why code needs care on a hosted builder

Squarespace manages hosting, updates and the editor, so your code sits inside a system you do not control. Careless code can break a mobile menu, slow every page or stop working when a layout is edited. Code pasted from forums often targets old versions of the editor and clashes with newer ones.

Tidy code avoids those traps. Selectors are specific, scripts load after the content, and every snippet is labelled so the next person knows what it does.

## How custom code improves the site

Code improves quality and usability more than raw numbers. A sticky announcement bar keeps an offer visible while people scroll. A filter lets visitors narrow a long gallery. A refined hover state tells people a card is clickable. A review or booking widget placed inside the page keeps visitors on your site instead of sending them away.

Because the code is small and tested, these features add little weight, and the speed check in the larger package confirms it.

## What good Squarespace code looks like

- Rules scoped to the page or block that needs them.
- Comments explaining each section in plain language.
- Fonts, colors and spacing based on your brand values.
- Scripts that wait for page content before running.
- Mobile and tablet rules written alongside desktop rules.
- Embeds from booking, review or map tools styled to fit.
- No duplicated libraries or unused snippets.
- Code kept in one documented place, not scattered across blocks.
- A short note on how to change colors or text later.

## What we do

We confirm what you want, find the cleanest place to add it and write the code. We then test it on a phone, a tablet and a desktop browser, and on the pages where it should not appear.

The Basic package covers one tweak or embed. Standard handles up to three changes, a hover or scroll effect, a third-party widget and editing notes. Premium builds larger features such as custom header behavior or data from an outside service, stores the code cleanly and compares speed before and after. We can also repair code a previous developer left behind.

## Do and avoid with custom code

**Do:**
- Describe the exact behavior you want, with examples from other sites.
- Keep a copy of any code you add.
- Test after every template or layout change.
- Ask us before adding another script.

**Avoid:**
- Pasting snippets you do not understand.
- Loading several libraries for one small effect.
- Editing code blocks that other people also manage.
- Assuming code will behave the same on every plan.

## Who this is for

A designer who needs exact typography and spacing will find the style panel limiting. A coach who wants a booking calendar inside a page needs a tidy embed. A business owner with a broken snippet from an earlier freelancer wants it repaired without a rebuild.

## What we need from you

Send the page addresses, a short description or screenshot of the result you want, and any existing code. We never need your password. Invite us as a contributor with the permissions needed to edit pages and code settings, and tell us if your plan limits custom code, so we can suggest a workable route.
